propositions: The test monolithically iterates 884 corpus units × 2 renderers, spawning ~1768 serial pandoc processes in a single test function, costing 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation, exceeding CI's 300s per-test timeout on contended macOS runners.

pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the xdist worker process outright with no traceback or test failure report, manifesting as 'node down: Not properly terminated' followed by worker crash attribution at session end.

The test must be chunk-parametrized into fixed-size batches (40 units per chunk) so per-test cost is bounded by construction rather than corpus size, enabling parallel execution across xdist workers and providing structural immunity to future corpus growth.

A coverage guard test must verify that all parametrized chunks concatenate to exactly _renderable_units() and total >= 100, preventing silent unit drops from the equivalence comparison while preserving the byte-identity property with real pandoc on both _convert and oracle paths.
